controls.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR/BOLA)

source_summary.what_it_is: The app lets a logged-in user access another user's records by changing an ID or reference.
source_summary.usual_cause: Authorization is checked only in the UI, or the server verifies login but not ownership/permission for the requested object.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may read, change, or delete other users' private data.
source_summary.prevention: Enforce object-level authorization on every server-side request. Derive the user from the trusted session, check ownership/role before every read/write, use deny-by-default policies, and test cross-account access.

signals: authenticated endpoints operate on user-owned records referenced by an id

required_evidence: server-side object ownership/permission check exists on every read/write route
cross-account negative access test (user A cannot access user B's object by id)

controls.title: Broken Function Level Authorization

source_summary.what_it_is: Users can call admin or privileged functions that their role should not be allowed to use.
source_summary.usual_cause: The frontend hides privileged buttons, but backend routes or server actions do not independently enforce roles/permissions.
source_summary.potential_impact: A normal account may perform administrative actions, change settings, manage users, or access restricted functions.
source_summary.prevention: Require server-side authorization for every privileged route/action. Centralize role/permission checks and default to deny.

signals: app has role-differentiated or privileged (admin/staff) routes or actions

required_evidence: server-side role/permission check exists on every privileged route, independent of UI
negative test proving a lower-privilege account is rejected from a privileged action

controls.title: Missing Authentication on Sensitive Endpoints

source_summary.what_it_is: Sensitive endpoints work without proving who the caller is.
source_summary.usual_cause: Developers expose internal routes, APIs, server actions, or functions without authentication middleware.
source_summary.potential_impact: Unauthenticated attackers may access data or perform protected actions.
source_summary.prevention: Require authentication on all non-public endpoints and explicitly document the small set of routes intended to be public.

signals: endpoints exist that return or mutate non-public data

required_evidence: every sensitive endpoint requires a valid authenticated session/token
unauthenticated request to a sensitive endpoint is rejected

controls.title: Privilege Escalation

source_summary.what_it_is: A lower-privileged user can gain permissions intended for admins or other trusted roles.
source_summary.usual_cause: Roles or permission fields can be changed by the client, mass-assigned, or insufficiently validated.
source_summary.potential_impact: An attacker may become an administrator or gain powerful account capabilities.
source_summary.prevention: Keep authorization data server-controlled. Restrict role changes to explicitly authorized admin workflows and validate transitions.

signals: app has more than one privilege/role level (user, admin, tenant-owner, etc.)

required_evidence: role/privilege assignment cannot be set or changed by the caller's own request
negative test proving a low-privilege account cannot elevate its own role

controls.title: Insecure Direct Database Access from Client

source_summary.what_it_is: The browser talks directly to database operations that are broader than the user's actual permissions.
source_summary.usual_cause: Database policies such as RLS are missing, incomplete, or bypassed while public client credentials can reach sensitive tables.
source_summary.potential_impact: Users may query or modify data outside their intended scope.
source_summary.prevention: Use strict database authorization policies, least-privilege client access, server-side operations for sensitive actions, and test policies with multiple identities.

signals: a frontend/browser/mobile client holds direct database connection credentials or an unrestricted client-side DB SDK key

required_evidence: no direct database connection string or unrestricted client DB key is shipped to a client build
data access from the client is mediated by a server-side API or a scoped, policy-enforced client SDK

controls.title: Exposed API Keys or Secrets in Frontend

source_summary.what_it_is: Private credentials are shipped in browser JavaScript, HTML, source maps, or public configuration.
source_summary.usual_cause: Secrets are placed in client environment variables or hard-coded into frontend code.
source_summary.potential_impact: Anyone can extract and abuse the credential, potentially causing data access, charges, or account compromise.
source_summary.prevention: Keep secrets server-side only, rotate exposed keys, use restricted credentials, and proxy privileged third-party calls through trusted backend code.

signals: a built frontend bundle exists

required_evidence: no third-party or backend secret key is present in shipped frontend/client bundle source
frontend build only contains publishable/public keys

controls.title: Hard-Coded Secrets in Source Code

source_summary.what_it_is: Passwords, tokens, signing keys, or credentials are embedded directly in application code or committed files.
source_summary.usual_cause: Developers hard-code secrets for convenience or commit local environment files.
source_summary.potential_impact: Repository access, logs, builds, or leaks can expose credentials.
source_summary.prevention: Store secrets in a proper secret manager or protected environment variables, remove them from history where necessary, and rotate compromised values.

signals: source repository exists

required_evidence: no credential/token/private-key literal is committed in source
secrets are loaded from environment/secret-manager configuration, not source

controls.title: SQL Injection

source_summary.what_it_is: Untrusted input changes the meaning of a SQL query.
source_summary.usual_cause: Queries are built by concatenating user input instead of using parameterized statements or a safe ORM.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may read, alter, or delete database data and sometimes bypass authentication.
source_summary.prevention: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements, safe ORM APIs, strict input handling, and least-privilege database accounts.

signals: app builds or executes SQL against a relational database

required_evidence: all SQL statements built from request-influenced input use parameterized queries/prepared statements or a query builder that never concatenates raw input
negative test proving an injection payload does not alter query behavior

controls.title: NoSQL Injection

source_summary.what_it_is: User input changes the structure or operators of a NoSQL query.
source_summary.usual_cause: Raw request objects or attacker-controlled operators are passed directly into database filters.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may bypass filters, authentication, or access unintended records.
source_summary.prevention: Build queries from explicitly allowed fields, validate types, reject unexpected operators/objects, and use safe driver APIs.

signals: app queries a NoSQL/document database (e.g. MongoDB) with request-influenced input

required_evidence: request-influenced input cannot be interpreted as query operators
negative test proving an operator-injection payload does not alter query behavior

controls.title: OS Command Injection

source_summary.what_it_is: User input becomes part of an operating-system command.
source_summary.usual_cause: The app uses shell commands with concatenated filenames, URLs, options, or other user-controlled values.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may execute commands on the server.
source_summary.prevention: Avoid shell execution when possible. Use safe library APIs; otherwise use argument arrays, strict allowlists, and a low-privilege runtime.

signals: app invokes a shell/OS command and includes any request-influenced input

required_evidence: no shell command is built via string concatenation/interpolation of request-influenced input
negative test proving a shell metacharacter payload does not execute unintended commands

controls.title: Server-Side Template Injection

source_summary.what_it_is: Attacker-controlled text is interpreted as template code on the server.
source_summary.usual_cause: User input is inserted into a server-side template in an executable/template-expression context.
source_summary.potential_impact: Depending on the engine, attackers may access server data or execute dangerous operations.
source_summary.prevention: Never evaluate user content as template source. Use fixed templates and pass untrusted values only as escaped data.

signals: app renders a server-side template engine with request-influenced input

required_evidence: request-influenced input is never rendered as template syntax (only as template data)
negative test proving a template-expression payload is not evaluated

controls.title: Cross-Site Scripting (Stored XSS)

source_summary.what_it_is: Malicious script-like content is saved by the app and later rendered to other users.
source_summary.usual_cause: Stored user content is inserted into HTML without context-appropriate escaping or safe sanitization.
source_summary.potential_impact: Visitors may have actions performed in their browser context or sensitive information exposed.
source_summary.prevention: Prefer output encoding. Sanitize only where rich HTML is intentionally supported, use a proven sanitizer, and enforce a strong CSP as defense in depth.

signals: app stores user-supplied content and later renders it to other users

required_evidence: stored user content is output-encoded or sanitized at render time
negative test proving a stored script payload does not execute in another user's session

controls.title: Cross-Site Scripting (Reflected XSS)

source_summary.what_it_is: Malicious input from a request is immediately reflected into a page in an executable context.
source_summary.usual_cause: Query parameters, errors, search terms, or other request data are rendered without safe encoding.
source_summary.potential_impact: A crafted link can cause script execution in a victim's browser.
source_summary.prevention: Use context-aware output encoding, safe framework rendering, and avoid unsafe HTML sinks.

signals: app reflects request input (query params, form fields) back into an HTML response

required_evidence: reflected request input is output-encoded at render time
negative test proving a reflected script payload does not execute

controls.title: DOM-Based XSS

source_summary.what_it_is: Client-side JavaScript takes attacker-controlled data and writes it into a dangerous DOM sink.
source_summary.usual_cause: Values from URLs, storage, messages, or APIs flow into innerHTML or similar unsafe browser APIs.
source_summary.potential_impact: Malicious links or data may trigger script execution in the browser.
source_summary.prevention: Use textContent/safe DOM APIs, sanitize intentionally allowed HTML, and validate message origins.

signals: client-side JavaScript writes request-influenced or URL-derived data into the DOM

required_evidence: no request-influenced/URL-derived value is written via an unsafe DOM sink (innerHTML, document.write, eval, etc.) without sanitization
negative test proving a crafted URL/fragment does not execute script in the browser

controls.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

source_summary.what_it_is: A user's browser can be tricked into sending an authenticated state-changing request from another site.
source_summary.usual_cause: Cookie-authenticated state changes lack CSRF defenses and accept cross-site requests.
source_summary.potential_impact: Victims may unknowingly change account data or perform sensitive actions.
source_summary.prevention: Use SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens where needed, Origin/Referer validation, and never use GET for state changes.

signals: app performs state-changing requests using cookie-based session authentication

required_evidence: state-changing requests require a CSRF token or an equivalent same-site/origin check
negative test proving a cross-origin forged request is rejected

controls.title: Weak Password Storage

source_summary.what_it_is: Passwords are stored in a form that is too easy to recover if the database leaks.
source_summary.usual_cause: Plaintext, reversible encryption, fast hashes, or weak password-hashing parameters are used.
source_summary.potential_impact: A database breach can expose users' passwords and reused credentials.
source_summary.prevention: Use a modern password hashing function such as Argon2id or a well-configured bcrypt/scrypt implementation with unique salts.

signals: app stores user passwords/credentials

required_evidence: passwords are hashed with a modern adaptive algorithm (bcrypt/argon2/scrypt) with per-user salt
no reversible encryption or fast general-purpose hash (md5/sha1/plain sha256) is used for password storage

controls.title: Weak Password Policy / Credential Abuse Exposure

source_summary.what_it_is: The app makes account takeover easier by allowing very weak credentials or failing to defend against common credential abuse.
source_summary.usual_cause: Poor password controls, no breached-password screening, and weak login protections.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers have an easier time taking over accounts with guessed or reused credentials.
source_summary.prevention: Allow long passphrases, block known compromised passwords where practical, support password managers, and combine with rate limiting/MFA.

signals: app has a self-service password-based signup/login flow

required_evidence: a minimum password strength requirement is enforced server-side
negative/abuse test proving repeated credential-stuffing attempts are throttled or blocked

controls.title: Missing Multi-Factor Authentication for Sensitive Accounts

source_summary.what_it_is: High-impact accounts rely on a single authentication factor.
source_summary.usual_cause: Admin, financial, developer, or other sensitive accounts have no MFA option or requirement.
source_summary.potential_impact: A stolen password alone may be enough for account takeover.
source_summary.prevention: Support phishing-resistant MFA where possible and require MFA for privileged accounts.

signals: app has privileged (admin/staff) or otherwise sensitive accounts

required_evidence: multi-factor authentication is available and enforceable for sensitive/privileged accounts
documented decision on which account tiers require MFA

controls.title: Session Fixation

source_summary.what_it_is: An attacker can cause a victim to authenticate using a session identifier the attacker already knows.
source_summary.usual_cause: The session ID is not regenerated after login or privilege changes.
source_summary.potential_impact: The attacker may reuse the known session to access the authenticated account.
source_summary.prevention: Rotate session identifiers after authentication and privilege changes; invalidate pre-authentication sessions.

signals: app uses a server-issued session identifier after login

required_evidence: a new session identifier is issued on privilege change (login, elevation)
negative test proving a pre-login session id is not reused as an authenticated session after login

controls.title: Session Hijacking Exposure

source_summary.what_it_is: Session tokens are easier to steal or reuse than they should be.
source_summary.usual_cause: Tokens are exposed to JavaScript unnecessarily, sent insecurely, logged, leaked in URLs, or have excessive lifetime.
source_summary.potential_impact: A stolen token may allow account takeover.
source_summary.prevention: Use Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies where appropriate, TLS, short reasonable lifetimes, rotation, revocation, and no tokens in URLs/logs.

signals: app uses session tokens/cookies to maintain authenticated state

required_evidence: session tokens are transmitted only over TLS and use Secure/HttpOnly cookie attributes
session invalidation on logout/timeout is enforced server-side

controls.title: JWT Signature Verification Errors

source_summary.what_it_is: The application accepts a JWT without correctly verifying that it was signed by a trusted issuer.
source_summary.usual_cause: Signature verification is disabled, algorithms are misconfigured, or untrusted keys/claims are accepted.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may forge identities or privileges.
source_summary.prevention: Use a maintained JWT library, pin expected algorithms, verify signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and required claims.

signals: app issues or accepts JWTs for authentication/authorization

required_evidence: JWT verification enforces a fixed, expected signing algorithm (no algorithm confusion, no 'none' algorithm accepted)
negative test proving a token with a forged/none-algorithm signature is rejected

controls.title: JWT Claims Trusted Without Authorization

source_summary.what_it_is: The server treats token claims as sufficient permission without applying current application authorization rules.
source_summary.usual_cause: Roles, tenant IDs, or permissions in tokens are stale, overly trusted, or accepted from untrusted sources.
source_summary.potential_impact: Users may retain or gain access they should not have.
source_summary.prevention: Verify trusted claims and still apply server-side authorization for the requested resource/action; keep sensitive authorization state current.

signals: app derives authorization decisions from JWT claims

required_evidence: authorization decisions are re-checked server-side against current state, not solely trusted from client-supplied claims
negative test proving a tampered/self-asserted claim does not grant unauthorized access

controls.title: OAuth Redirect URI Weakness

source_summary.what_it_is: An OAuth flow can redirect authorization results to an attacker-controlled or unintended destination.
source_summary.usual_cause: Redirect URIs are matched loosely, dynamically accepted, or built from user input.
source_summary.potential_impact: Authorization codes or tokens may be exposed to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
source_summary.prevention: Use exact registered redirect URIs and strict provider configuration; never accept arbitrary redirect destinations.

signals: app implements an OAuth/OIDC authorization flow

required_evidence: redirect_uri is validated against an exact allow-list server-side
negative test proving an unregistered or wildcard-manipulated redirect_uri is rejected

controls.title: OAuth State/PKCE Validation Missing

source_summary.what_it_is: OAuth login lacks protections that bind the authorization response to the initiating browser/client.
source_summary.usual_cause: The app omits or incorrectly validates state and, for applicable public clients, PKCE.
source_summary.potential_impact: Login CSRF, authorization response mix-ups, or code interception risks increase.
source_summary.prevention: Generate unpredictable state, validate it once, use PKCE with S256 where applicable, and follow the provider/library's secure flow.

signals: app implements an OAuth/OIDC authorization code flow

required_evidence: state parameter and, for public clients, PKCE are generated, transmitted, and validated on callback
negative test proving a callback with a missing/mismatched state or PKCE verifier is rejected

controls.title: Account Enumeration

source_summary.what_it_is: The app reveals whether a username, email, or account exists.
source_summary.usual_cause: Login, registration, password reset, or invitation responses differ in text, status, or timing.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers can build lists of valid accounts for targeted attacks.
source_summary.prevention: Use consistent public responses and reasonable timing while still logging detailed internal outcomes.

signals: app exposes a login, signup, or password-reset flow

required_evidence: authentication-adjacent responses (login, signup, reset) do not differ in a way that reveals account existence
negative test comparing responses for existing vs non-existing accounts

controls.title: Brute-Force Login Protection Missing

source_summary.what_it_is: Attackers can make large numbers of authentication attempts without meaningful resistance.
source_summary.usual_cause: No rate limiting, progressive delays, anomaly controls, or MFA protection exists.
source_summary.potential_impact: Passwords are easier to guess or test at scale.
source_summary.prevention: Rate-limit by multiple signals, add progressive delays/risk controls, protect against distributed abuse, and avoid permanent lockouts that enable denial of service.

signals: app has a password-based login endpoint

required_evidence: failed login attempts are rate-limited or lockout/backoff is applied per account/IP
test proving repeated failed login attempts are throttled or blocked

controls.title: Password Reset Token Weakness

source_summary.what_it_is: Password reset tokens can be guessed, reused, leaked, or remain valid too long.
source_summary.usual_cause: Tokens have low entropy, are stored insecurely, are not single-use, or are not invalidated after reset.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may reset another user's password.
source_summary.prevention: Use cryptographically random, short-lived, single-use tokens, store only safe representations, and invalidate sessions as appropriate after reset.

signals: app has a self-service password reset flow

required_evidence: reset tokens are high-entropy, single-use, and time-limited, validated server-side
negative test proving an expired, reused, or guessed reset token is rejected

controls.title: Email Verification Bypass

source_summary.what_it_is: A user can obtain verified-account privileges without actually proving control of the email address.
source_summary.usual_cause: Verification state can be client-controlled, tokens are weak/reusable, or protected features do not check verified status.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may create trusted-looking or privileged accounts using addresses they do not control.
source_summary.prevention: Keep verification state server-controlled and use secure, expiring, single-use verification tokens.

signals: app requires email verification before granting account access/trust

required_evidence: verification status is enforced server-side before granting the gated capability
negative test proving an unverified account cannot access the gated capability by manipulating client state

controls.title: Insecure 'Remember Me' Tokens

source_summary.what_it_is: Long-lived login tokens can be stolen, predicted, or reused indefinitely.
source_summary.usual_cause: Persistent tokens are weak, stored plaintext server-side, never rotated, or not revocable.
source_summary.potential_impact: A stolen persistent token may provide long-term account access.
source_summary.prevention: Use high-entropy tokens, store hashed token values, rotate on use, expire them, support revocation, and bind carefully to account/session state.

signals: app offers a persistent/'remember me' login option

required_evidence: remember-me tokens are high-entropy, stored hashed, single-use or rotated, and independently revocable

controls.title: Insecure Cookie Attributes

source_summary.what_it_is: Authentication or sensitive cookies lack browser protections.
source_summary.usual_cause: Secure, HttpOnly, or appropriate SameSite attributes are missing or cookie scope is unnecessarily broad.
source_summary.potential_impact: Cookies are more exposed to interception, scripts, or cross-site requests.
source_summary.prevention: Set Secure and HttpOnly for session cookies, choose appropriate SameSite, minimize Domain/Path scope, and use HTTPS.

signals: app sets authentication or session cookies

required_evidence: session/auth cookies are set with Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite attribute
response inspection confirms the attributes are actually delivered at runtime

controls.title: CORS Misconfiguration

source_summary.what_it_is: The server allows untrusted websites to make browser requests that should be restricted.
source_summary.usual_cause: Origins are reflected blindly, wildcards are used with sensitive data, or credentials are allowed too broadly.
source_summary.potential_impact: A malicious site may interact with authenticated APIs or read data when browser credentials are included.
source_summary.prevention: Use a strict allowlist of trusted origins, never reflect arbitrary origins, and enable credentials only where required.

signals: app serves a cross-origin-callable API

required_evidence: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is not a reflected wildcard combined with credentials
negative test proving an untrusted origin cannot read credentialed cross-origin responses

controls.title: Missing or Weak Content Security Policy

source_summary.what_it_is: The browser has little defense in depth against injected scripts or unsafe content sources.
source_summary.usual_cause: CSP is absent or uses overly broad sources such as unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval without necessity.
source_summary.potential_impact: XSS and third-party script compromise can have greater impact.
source_summary.prevention: Deploy a restrictive CSP tailored to the app, preferably using nonces/hashes for scripts, and test in report-only mode before enforcement.

signals: app serves HTML responses to a browser

required_evidence: a Content-Security-Policy header is present and restricts script sources
response inspection confirms the header is actually delivered at runtime

controls.title: Clickjacking

source_summary.what_it_is: An attacker can embed the app in a frame and trick a user into clicking hidden or disguised controls.
source_summary.usual_cause: The application does not restrict framing.
source_summary.potential_impact: Users may unknowingly trigger sensitive actions.
source_summary.prevention: Use CSP frame-ancestors and, for legacy support where needed, X-Frame-Options.

signals: app serves HTML pages that perform sensitive actions

required_evidence: X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors prevents the sensitive page from being framed
response inspection confirms the protection is actually delivered at runtime

controls.title: Open Redirect

source_summary.what_it_is: The application redirects users to attacker-chosen external URLs.
source_summary.usual_cause: Redirect destinations are taken directly from query parameters or user input.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers can abuse trusted links for phishing or authorization-flow problems.
source_summary.prevention: Use relative internal destinations or a strict allowlist; never redirect directly to arbitrary user-supplied URLs.

signals: app redirects based on a request-supplied URL/parameter

required_evidence: redirect targets are validated against an allow-list or restricted to relative paths
negative test proving an attacker-supplied external redirect target is rejected

controls.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

source_summary.what_it_is: The server fetches a URL chosen by a user, allowing access to destinations the user could not reach directly.
source_summary.usual_cause: URL fetchers, webhooks, image importers, previews, or integrations accept arbitrary destinations without network restrictions.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may reach internal services, cloud metadata, or sensitive network resources.
source_summary.prevention: Allowlist destinations where possible, block private/link-local/loopback ranges after DNS resolution, restrict protocols, control redirects, and isolate outbound networking.

signals: server makes outbound HTTP/network requests to a URL influenced by request input

required_evidence: outbound request targets are validated/allow-listed and internal/metadata address ranges are blocked
negative test proving a request targeting an internal address is rejected

controls.title: Path Traversal

source_summary.what_it_is: User input manipulates a file path to access files outside the intended directory.
source_summary.usual_cause: Filenames or paths are concatenated without canonicalization and containment checks.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may read or overwrite sensitive files.
source_summary.prevention: Use generated identifiers, safe storage APIs, canonicalize paths, and verify the final path remains inside the allowed base directory.

signals: server reads/writes a filesystem path influenced by request input

required_evidence: file paths built from request input are normalized/validated against a restricted base directory
negative test proving a traversal payload (e.g. ../) cannot escape the intended directory

controls.title: Local File Inclusion / Unsafe File Loading

source_summary.what_it_is: The app loads local files or modules based on user-controlled values.
source_summary.usual_cause: Dynamic include/template/file-loading functions receive untrusted paths.
source_summary.potential_impact: Sensitive files may be disclosed or unsafe content executed depending on the runtime.
source_summary.prevention: Use fixed mappings/allowlists instead of user-controlled paths and remove dynamic include behavior.

signals: server loads/includes a file or module whose path is influenced by request input

required_evidence: file/module inclusion is restricted to a fixed allow-list, never a raw request-supplied path
negative test proving an attacker-supplied path cannot cause inclusion of an arbitrary file

controls.title: Unrestricted File Upload

source_summary.what_it_is: Users can upload files that the application treats as executable or otherwise dangerous.
source_summary.usual_cause: The server trusts extensions/MIME types, stores uploads in executable locations, or lacks content and size restrictions.
source_summary.potential_impact: Uploads may lead to malware hosting, code execution, XSS, storage abuse, or data exposure.
source_summary.prevention: Allow only necessary file types, validate content, rename files, store outside executable web roots, limit size, and serve with safe headers.

signals: app accepts user file uploads

required_evidence: uploaded files are validated (type/size/content) and stored outside the web/execution root or with execution disabled
negative test proving an executable/script file upload is rejected or rendered inert

controls.title: File Upload Content-Type Confusion

source_summary.what_it_is: A file is validated or served as one type but interpreted by the browser or downstream system as another.
source_summary.usual_cause: The app trusts MIME headers/extensions or allows browser content sniffing.
source_summary.potential_impact: Uploaded content may execute in a browser or bypass validation.
source_summary.prevention: Validate actual file format, set explicit response Content-Type, use nosniff, and force download when active content is not intended.

signals: app accepts user file uploads and trusts a file type for handling

required_evidence: file type is verified by content inspection, not solely by client-supplied Content-Type or extension
negative test proving a mislabeled file (wrong extension/Content-Type) is rejected or handled safely

controls.title: Insecure File Permissions / Public Storage

source_summary.what_it_is: Sensitive files are accessible to users or the public because storage permissions are too broad.
source_summary.usual_cause: Cloud buckets, object storage, directories, or generated links default to public or have weak policies.
source_summary.potential_impact: Private documents, videos, backups, or user uploads may leak.
source_summary.prevention: Make storage private by default, authorize every access, use short-lived signed URLs where appropriate, and audit bucket policies.

signals: app stores uploaded or generated files in cloud storage or on a filesystem

required_evidence: storage bucket/object permissions default to private with explicit, scoped grants for anything public
negative test proving a private object cannot be fetched without authorization

controls.title: Mass Assignment

source_summary.what_it_is: Attackers can set fields that the UI never intended them to control.
source_summary.usual_cause: The backend binds entire request objects directly to database models or update operations.
source_summary.potential_impact: Users may change roles, ownership, prices, status flags, balances, or other protected fields.
source_summary.prevention: Explicitly allowlist writable fields for each operation and keep sensitive fields server-controlled.

signals: app accepts a JSON/form body and binds it to a model/record

required_evidence: request bodies are bound through an explicit allow-list of mutable fields, never bulk-assigned to the full model
negative test proving a privileged/protected field cannot be set via unexpected request body fields

controls.title: Parameter Tampering

source_summary.what_it_is: The server trusts values from the browser that should be calculated or controlled server-side.
source_summary.usual_cause: Prices, discounts, user IDs, plan names, permissions, quantities, or workflow states are accepted directly from client requests.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may manipulate transactions or application state.
source_summary.prevention: Treat client values as untrusted; derive security- and money-sensitive values from server-side records and validated rules.

signals: app trusts a client-supplied parameter (price, quantity, role, id) for a server-side decision

required_evidence: security- or business-relevant values are re-derived/validated server-side, not trusted from client parameters
negative test proving a tampered parameter does not change the server-side outcome

controls.title: Business Logic Abuse

source_summary.what_it_is: A user follows technically valid requests in an unintended sequence to gain an unfair or unauthorized result.
source_summary.usual_cause: Security is implemented per endpoint but not across the full business workflow.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may bypass limits, duplicate benefits, skip required steps, or manipulate transactions.
source_summary.prevention: Model allowed workflow states and invariants server-side, validate transitions, and test abuse cases rather than only malformed input.

signals: app has multi-step workflows or state transitions with business rules (e.g. coupons, quotas, order flow)
applicability.notes: Abuse-case enumeration is workflow-specific and generally requires human judgment to define before it can be tested.

required_evidence: documented abuse-case analysis for the workflow's state transitions
test proving an out-of-order or repeated abuse of the workflow does not bypass its business rule

controls.title: Race Condition / Double Submission

source_summary.what_it_is: Two or more concurrent requests cause an operation to happen more than once or violate an invariant.
source_summary.usual_cause: Critical operations lack transactions, locking, idempotency, or unique constraints.
source_summary.potential_impact: Users may receive duplicate credits, orders, bookings, withdrawals, or other unintended results.
source_summary.prevention: Use database transactions/constraints, atomic operations, idempotency keys, and concurrency-safe state changes.

signals: app has an endpoint whose repeated/concurrent invocation could double-spend, double-redeem, or double-create a resource

required_evidence: concurrent-request test proving repeated simultaneous submissions cannot bypass a one-time/limited-use constraint

controls.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Sensitive APIs

source_summary.what_it_is: An endpoint can be called excessively without controls.
source_summary.usual_cause: No server-side quotas exist for expensive, sensitive, or abuse-prone operations.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may brute force, scrape, spam, cause excessive costs, or degrade service.
source_summary.prevention: Apply endpoint-specific rate limits and quotas using appropriate identity/network signals and return safe retry behavior.

signals: app exposes a sensitive or expensive API endpoint (auth, payments, search, AI calls)

required_evidence: sensitive endpoints enforce a rate limit or quota
test proving repeated rapid requests are throttled or rejected

controls.title: Resource Exhaustion / Unbounded Requests

source_summary.what_it_is: A user can force the app to consume excessive CPU, memory, bandwidth, storage, or third-party spend.
source_summary.usual_cause: Requests lack limits on payload size, pagination, query complexity, processing time, uploads, or generated output.
source_summary.potential_impact: The service may become slow, unavailable, or unexpectedly expensive.
source_summary.prevention: Set strict practical limits, timeouts, pagination caps, concurrency controls, and budgets for expensive operations.

signals: app accepts requests whose size/complexity/duration is not bounded

required_evidence: request size, pagination, and processing time are bounded server-side
test proving an oversized/unbounded request is rejected rather than exhausting resources

controls.title: GraphQL Excessive Query Complexity

source_summary.what_it_is: Clients can submit GraphQL queries that consume excessive resources or expose more data than intended.
source_summary.usual_cause: Depth, complexity, batching, introspection, field authorization, or pagination are poorly controlled.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may cause denial of service or retrieve excessive data.
source_summary.prevention: Enforce field-level authorization, depth/complexity limits, pagination, batching controls, and production-appropriate introspection settings.

signals: app exposes a GraphQL server

required_evidence: query depth/complexity/cost limiting is enforced server-side
test proving a deeply nested or high-cost query is rejected rather than executed

controls.title: Excessive Data Exposure

source_summary.what_it_is: APIs return more fields than the client actually needs.
source_summary.usual_cause: Entire database records or sensitive internal fields are serialized by default.
source_summary.potential_impact: Private data, internal identifiers, secrets, or metadata may leak.
source_summary.prevention: Use explicit response schemas/DTOs and return only the fields required for the feature.

signals: an API response is built by serializing an internal model/object
applicability.notes: What counts as 'excessive' for a given field is contextual to the product/business, so a full determination needs human review beyond schema inspection.

required_evidence: API responses are built from an explicit response schema/DTO, not a raw serialized internal model
review confirming no field beyond what the specific consumer needs is present in the response

controls.title: Sensitive Data in URLs

source_summary.what_it_is: Secrets or private data appear in URL paths or query strings.
source_summary.usual_cause: Tokens, emails, personal data, or credentials are passed through GET parameters.
source_summary.potential_impact: URLs may be stored in browser history, logs, analytics, referrers, screenshots, and proxies.
source_summary.prevention: Keep sensitive values out of URLs; use request bodies or secure cookies/headers as appropriate and redact logging.

signals: app includes any identifier or credential-like value in a URL/query string

required_evidence: no session token, password, or other sensitive value is passed via URL/query string

controls.title: Sensitive Data in Logs

source_summary.what_it_is: Logs contain secrets or personal information that should not be recorded.
source_summary.usual_cause: The app logs full request bodies, headers, tokens, passwords, payment data, or sensitive user records.
source_summary.potential_impact: Anyone with log access may gain credentials or private data.
source_summary.prevention: Use structured logging with explicit redaction/allowlists and minimize sensitive data retention.

signals: app writes application/request logs

required_evidence: logging code does not record passwords, tokens, full payment card numbers, or other sensitive fields

controls.title: Verbose Error Messages

source_summary.what_it_is: Production errors reveal internal details useful to attackers.
source_summary.usual_cause: Stack traces, SQL errors, file paths, environment details, or framework debug pages are returned to users.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers gain information about the application's internals.
source_summary.prevention: Return generic public errors with correlation IDs while recording detailed diagnostics only in protected logs.

signals: app returns error responses to clients

required_evidence: production error responses do not include stack traces, internal paths, or raw exception detail

controls.title: Debug Mode Enabled in Production

source_summary.what_it_is: Development features expose internals or unsafe controls in the live application.
source_summary.usual_cause: Debug flags, developer consoles, test routes, profilers, or verbose framework modes remain enabled.
source_summary.potential_impact: Sensitive information or powerful debugging capabilities may be exposed.
source_summary.prevention: Use environment-specific configuration and fail production builds/deployments if debug features are enabled.

signals: app has a framework debug/development mode flag

required_evidence: production deployment configuration disables framework debug/development mode

controls.title: Security Misconfigured HTTP Headers

source_summary.what_it_is: Important browser security controls are missing or incorrectly configured.
source_summary.usual_cause: Headers such as HSTS, CSP, nosniff, frame protections, and referrer policy are absent or overly permissive.
source_summary.potential_impact: Browser-based attacks or information leakage may be easier.
source_summary.prevention: Set appropriate security headers centrally and test them in production-like environments.

signals: app serves HTTP responses to a browser client

required_evidence: baseline security headers (e.g. X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy) are set
response inspection confirms the headers are actually delivered at runtime

controls.title: TLS / HTTPS Misconfiguration

source_summary.what_it_is: Sensitive traffic is not consistently protected in transit.
source_summary.usual_cause: HTTP remains available for authenticated traffic, certificates/configuration are weak, or secure redirects/HSTS are missing.
source_summary.potential_impact: Credentials and private data may be exposed or modified in transit.
source_summary.prevention: Require HTTPS, use modern TLS configuration, redirect HTTP safely, and enable HSTS after confirming HTTPS coverage.

signals: app is served over a network to end users

required_evidence: all endpoints are served over TLS with HTTP redirected/upgraded to HTTPS
live TLS handshake/cert-chain inspection confirms a valid, current configuration

controls.title: Weak Cryptography / Custom Crypto

source_summary.what_it_is: Sensitive data is protected with obsolete algorithms, weak modes, predictable randomness, or home-grown cryptography.
source_summary.usual_cause: Developers implement encryption/signing themselves or use outdated primitives/configuration.
source_summary.potential_impact: Protected data may be recoverable or signatures/tokens forgeable.
source_summary.prevention: Use maintained cryptographic libraries and modern authenticated encryption/signature primitives with secure key management.

signals: app performs encryption/signing/hashing of sensitive data itself

required_evidence: cryptographic operations use vetted standard-library/well-known algorithms and libraries, not a custom-designed cipher/scheme

controls.title: Insecure Randomness

source_summary.what_it_is: Security-sensitive values are predictable.
source_summary.usual_cause: Normal pseudo-random functions are used for tokens, codes, session IDs, or reset links.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may guess security tokens.
source_summary.prevention: Use the platform's cryptographically secure random generator with sufficient entropy.

signals: app generates a token, id, or secret value used for a security-relevant purpose

required_evidence: security-relevant random values are generated with a cryptographically secure random source, not a general-purpose PRNG

controls.title: Improper Certificate Validation

source_summary.what_it_is: The application accepts an untrusted TLS certificate when connecting to another service.
source_summary.usual_cause: Certificate or hostname verification is disabled to make development/integration easier.
source_summary.potential_impact: A network attacker may impersonate the remote service.
source_summary.prevention: Keep certificate and hostname validation enabled; install proper CA certificates instead of disabling verification.

signals: app makes outbound TLS connections (to APIs, databases, or other services)

required_evidence: outbound TLS clients do not disable certificate/hostname validation
negative test proving a connection to an endpoint with an invalid certificate is rejected

controls.title: Insecure Deserialization

source_summary.what_it_is: Untrusted serialized data is converted into application objects in a way that can trigger unsafe behavior.
source_summary.usual_cause: Dangerous native serialization formats or polymorphic object creation are used on attacker-controlled data.
source_summary.potential_impact: Depending on the technology, attackers may alter application state or trigger code execution.
source_summary.prevention: Prefer simple data formats such as JSON with strict schemas; never deserialize untrusted native objects; allowlist types if unavoidable.

signals: app deserializes data from an untrusted source (request body, message queue, uploaded file)

required_evidence: deserialization of untrusted input uses a safe/restricted format or schema, not an unrestricted native object deserializer
negative test proving a crafted serialized payload does not achieve code execution or object injection

controls.title: Prototype Pollution

source_summary.what_it_is: Attacker-controlled object keys modify JavaScript object prototypes or inherited properties.
source_summary.usual_cause: Unsafe deep merge, object assignment, query parsing, or vulnerable libraries accept keys such as __proto__ or constructor.prototype.
source_summary.potential_impact: Application logic may be corrupted and, in some contexts, security controls bypassed.
source_summary.prevention: Update vulnerable libraries, reject dangerous keys, use safe merge utilities, and avoid merging untrusted objects into security-sensitive configuration.

signals: app merges/assigns request-influenced keys into a JavaScript object

required_evidence: object merge/assignment code guards against __proto__/constructor/prototype keys
negative test proving a polluting payload does not alter the object prototype

controls.title: Dependency With Known Vulnerabilities

source_summary.what_it_is: The application uses a third-party package with a publicly known security flaw.
source_summary.usual_cause: Dependencies are outdated, unmaintained, pinned carelessly, or never scanned.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may exploit the vulnerable component through the application.
source_summary.prevention: Maintain lockfiles, scan dependencies, patch promptly based on reachability/severity, and remove abandoned packages.

signals: project declares third-party dependencies via a package manifest

required_evidence: dependency manifest/lockfile is scanned against a known-vulnerability database with no unresolved critical/high finding

controls.title: Malicious or Compromised Dependency

source_summary.what_it_is: A package or update contains intentionally harmful code or has been compromised upstream.
source_summary.usual_cause: Developers install unverified packages, typosquatted names, or automatically accept risky updates.
source_summary.potential_impact: Build systems, secrets, production data, or users may be compromised.
source_summary.prevention: Minimize dependencies, verify package identity/provenance, lock versions, review major changes, restrict install scripts, and protect CI secrets.

signals: project declares third-party dependencies via a package manifest
applicability.notes: Confirming malicious intent (vs. a benign vulnerability) generally exceeds what an automated scanner can conclude alone.

required_evidence: dependency provenance/integrity is checked (lockfile hash pinning, publisher reputation)
review of newly-added or recently-changed dependencies for signs of compromise

controls.title: Dependency Confusion

source_summary.what_it_is: A build installs an attacker-controlled public package instead of the intended private package.
source_summary.usual_cause: Private package names overlap with public registries and registry precedence/scoping is misconfigured.
source_summary.potential_impact: Malicious code may run during build or deployment.
source_summary.prevention: Use scoped private packages, explicit registry configuration, lockfiles, and controlled package publishing.

signals: project resolves internal/private package names from a public package registry

required_evidence: internal/private package names are published to a private/scoped registry or otherwise reserved so a public package of the same name cannot be resolved instead

controls.title: Exposed Source Maps / Build Artifacts

source_summary.what_it_is: Production publishes development artifacts that reveal source code, paths, or internal structure.
source_summary.usual_cause: Source maps, debug bundles, backup files, or build metadata are deployed publicly.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers gain easier insight into application internals and sometimes secrets accidentally embedded in builds.
source_summary.prevention: Do not publish unnecessary source maps/artifacts publicly; if source maps are needed for monitoring, keep them private with the monitoring provider.

signals: project builds a frontend bundle with a build tool that can emit source maps

required_evidence: production build does not publish source maps or other build artifacts (README fragments, .git) alongside the deployed bundle
negative test proving a source-map/build-artifact URL is not publicly fetchable in production

controls.title: Exposed .env, Git, Backup, or Config Files

source_summary.what_it_is: Sensitive project files are reachable from the public web server.
source_summary.usual_cause: Deployment copies hidden files, backups, repositories, or configuration into the served directory.
source_summary.potential_impact: Secrets, source code, or configuration may leak.
source_summary.prevention: Keep sensitive files outside the web root, block dotfiles/backups, and configure deployment allowlists.

signals: app is deployed behind a public web server

required_evidence: deployment excludes .env, .git, backup, and config files from the public web root
negative test proving common sensitive file paths (.env, .git/config, backup archives) are not publicly fetchable

controls.title: Cloud / Database Service Role Key Exposure

source_summary.what_it_is: A highly privileged cloud or backend key is exposed to untrusted clients.
source_summary.usual_cause: Service-role/admin credentials are placed in frontend code, mobile/browser configuration, logs, or public repositories.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may bypass normal access controls and gain broad backend access.
source_summary.prevention: Keep service/admin keys server-only, rotate exposed keys, and use public/anon keys only with strong backend policies.

signals: app uses a cloud provider or database service that issues an elevated/service-role key

required_evidence: service-role/elevated keys are never shipped to a client build or committed to source, only used server-side

controls.title: Database Row-Level Security Misconfiguration

source_summary.what_it_is: Database-level access policies allow users to read or modify rows they should not access.
source_summary.usual_cause: RLS is disabled, policies use overly broad conditions, or write checks are missing.
source_summary.potential_impact: Cross-user or cross-tenant data exposure and modification may occur.
source_summary.prevention: Enable RLS where applicable, define explicit SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies, use correct USING/WITH CHECK semantics, and test with multiple users.

signals: app uses a database with row-level security policies (e.g. Postgres RLS/Supabase)

required_evidence: row-level security is enabled on tables containing user-scoped data, with policies enforced at the database layer
runtime test with multiple identities proving one user's database session cannot read/write another user's rows

controls.title: Multi-Tenant Data Isolation Failure

source_summary.what_it_is: One organization's users can access another organization's data.
source_summary.usual_cause: Tenant identifiers are trusted from the client or not included consistently in authorization/database policies.
source_summary.potential_impact: A single customer may expose or modify another customer's data.
source_summary.prevention: Derive tenant membership from trusted server/session data and enforce tenant isolation at every data-access layer.

signals: organizations/workspaces/tenants share an application data plane

required_evidence: every data access path filters by the caller's tenant, enforced server-side or at the database layer
cross-tenant negative access test proving tenant A cannot read/write tenant B's data

controls.title: Webhook Signature Verification Missing

source_summary.what_it_is: The app accepts webhook requests without proving they came from the real provider.
source_summary.usual_cause: Webhook signatures/secrets are ignored or verified incorrectly.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may forge events such as payments, subscriptions, or account changes.
source_summary.prevention: Use the provider's official signature-verification method on the raw request body, reject invalid/timestamp-stale events, and protect against replay.

signals: app receives inbound webhooks from a third-party provider

required_evidence: inbound webhook handler verifies the provider's signature before processing the payload
negative test proving a request with a missing/invalid signature is rejected

controls.title: Webhook Replay / Duplicate Processing

source_summary.what_it_is: A valid webhook can be resent and processed multiple times.
source_summary.usual_cause: Events are not deduplicated or state changes are not idempotent.
source_summary.potential_impact: Payments, credits, emails, or other actions may happen repeatedly.
source_summary.prevention: Store provider event IDs, process idempotently, use unique constraints/transactions, and safely acknowledge duplicates.

signals: app receives inbound webhooks from a third-party provider

required_evidence: webhook processing is idempotent, keyed on a unique event id
replay test proving the same webhook event delivered twice does not double-apply its effect

controls.title: Payment Amount / Price Tampering

source_summary.what_it_is: The backend trusts a price or total supplied by the browser.
source_summary.usual_cause: Checkout requests accept client-calculated amounts, discounts, currency, or product prices.
source_summary.potential_impact: Attackers may pay less than intended or obtain incorrect entitlements.
source_summary.prevention: Look up product/price data server-side and create payment sessions from trusted records; verify completed events before granting access.

signals: app has a checkout/payment flow where a client influences an amount or price

required_evidence: the charged amount/price is computed and verified server-side from trusted data, never trusted from a client-supplied value
negative test in a payment provider sandbox proving a tampered client-side amount does not change the amount actually charged

controls.title: Payment Webhook / Entitlement Logic Failure

source_summary.what_it_is: The app grants paid access based on an untrusted browser response or incomplete payment state.
source_summary.usual_cause: Success pages, client callbacks, or loosely validated webhook fields directly activate subscriptions/products.
source_summary.potential_impact: Users may obtain paid features without a valid completed payment.
source_summary.prevention: Use verified server-side provider events as the source of truth and map them to known orders/customers.

signals: app grants entitlements/access based on a payment provider webhook event

required_evidence: entitlement is granted only after the provider webhook signature and event state are verified server-side
negative test in a payment provider sandbox proving a forged/failed-payment event does not grant entitlement

controls.title: Insecure API Key Authentication

source_summary.what_it_is: An API key is treated as a permanent password without sufficient protection or scope.
source_summary.usual_cause: Keys are long-lived, broadly privileged, stored plaintext, sent in URLs, or cannot be revoked.
source_summary.potential_impact: A leaked key may provide broad persistent access.
source_summary.prevention: Generate high-entropy keys, show once, store hashed values, scope permissions, support rotation/revocation, and transmit only over HTTPS headers.

signals: app authenticates API clients using a static API key

required_evidence: API keys are transmitted over TLS only, stored hashed server-side, and independently revocable
negative test proving a revoked/invalid API key is rejected

controls.title: Missing API Authorization Scope Checks

source_summary.what_it_is: An authenticated API credential can perform actions outside its intended scope.
source_summary.usual_cause: The server verifies that a token/key is valid but does not enforce scopes/permissions per endpoint.
source_summary.potential_impact: Integrations or leaked tokens gain excessive capabilities.
source_summary.prevention: Define least-privilege scopes and enforce required scopes server-side on every endpoint.

signals: app issues API keys/tokens with different scopes/permissions

required_evidence: each API endpoint checks the caller's token scope, not merely that a token is valid
negative test proving a token without the required scope is rejected by a scope-restricted endpoint

controls.title: Insecure AI/LLM Tool Authorization

source_summary.what_it_is: An AI feature can invoke tools or backend actions with more authority than the requesting user should have.
source_summary.usual_cause: The model is trusted to decide permissions, or tools run with broad service credentials without per-user authorization.
source_summary.potential_impact: Prompt manipulation or model mistakes may cause unauthorized data access or actions.
source_summary.prevention: Treat the model as untrusted orchestration. Enforce normal server-side authorization inside every tool/action and minimize tool privileges.

signals: app gives an LLM/agent the ability to call tools or access data on a user's behalf
applicability.notes: Model output is untrusted. Authorization must be enforced outside the model; a system prompt restricting tool use is not itself a security boundary.

required_evidence: tool-call authorization is enforced by code outside the model, using the caller's real permissions, not the model's own output
negative test proving a tool call the model attempts outside the caller's authorization is rejected by the enforcement layer, not merely discouraged by a prompt

controls.title: Prompt Injection Causing Unsafe Tool Use

source_summary.what_it_is: Untrusted content manipulates an AI feature into ignoring intended instructions or attempting unsafe actions.
source_summary.usual_cause: The app gives an LLM access to tools/data and assumes prompts alone are a security boundary.
source_summary.potential_impact: The model may attempt unauthorized tool calls, disclose data it was given, or take unintended actions.
source_summary.prevention: Do not rely on system prompts for authorization. Isolate untrusted content, constrain tools, validate outputs, and enforce permissions outside the model.

signals: app feeds untrusted content (user input, retrieved documents, tool output) into an LLM that can call tools or take actions
applicability.notes: A prevention prompt telling the model to ignore injected instructions is source material, not proof; enforcement must happen outside model reasoning.

required_evidence: untrusted content is isolated from trusted instructions and cannot itself grant tool permissions
negative test proving injected instructions embedded in untrusted content do not result in an unauthorized tool call
